newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court upholds social funds to Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds social funds to Portugal.

text.p: The European Court of Justice upheld on Thursday a ruling by the Court of First Instance (CFI) which refused to reduce the amount of social funds granted to several Portugese vocational training projects.

The CFI annulled a decision by the European Commission to reduce the funds, finding the application for annulment was timely and that Portugal had responded with certainty and clarity to questions posed by the Commission.

The Commission argued that it had notified its decision to the recipients of the funds. But the court said a notification of its decision was not enough unless it gave a detailed account of the decision's contents and reasoning.
In the absence of such detail, the party concerned would be denied precise knowledge of the contents of the act in question, making it difficult to effectively challenge the decision, the court said.

The Commission also challenged the CFI's finding that Portugal was not given adequate opportunity to comment prior to adoption of the decision. The court said it could not review this as it was not presented as an error of law.
(Court translation of the case. Original language of the case: Portuguese)
"Appeal - European Social Fund - Time-limit for bringing proceedings - Infringement of essential procedural requirements"
